    "Torah scrolls and all pre-Masoretic manuscripts (Qumran) are purely consonantal; systematic Tiberian pointing was added only in the 7th–10th centuries CE",

    "Apostolic citation of Psalm 40:6 via the LXX (‘a body you prepared me’) against the later pointed Hebrew (‘my ears you have opened’) treats the pre-Masoretic reading as Scripture",
    "Concrete examples (חלב milk/fat; Ps 22 kaʾaru ‘pierced’ vs kaʾari ‘like a lion’) show that identical consonants admit different vocalizations already attested in the LXX and Judean desert scrolls",

  ],
